skill: Compute a two-term indefinite integral using the sum rule and the power rule, rewriting radicals and reciprocals as rational powers where needed.
learner_operation: Read both signed summands, identify their exponents, increase each exponent by one and divide by the new exponent, then combine both antiderivatives and one arbitrary constant. For radio, distinguish this result from errors in signs, powers, factors or constants.
reasoning_steps: Identify the integration variable and both signed summands.
Rewrite radical/reciprocal summands as powers; represent constants with exponent zero.
Apply the sum/difference rule and integrate each summand with p -> p+1 and coefficient 1/(p+1).
Simplify rational coefficients and return one arbitrary constant, or the expression only if +C is printed outside the blank.

response_contract.observed: Five-choice math radio banks for q-2159, q-29828, q-71169, q-71167; single math blank excluding displayed +C for q-133291. Other captured examples lack answer fields.
response_contract.difficulty: Moderate includes reciprocal radical plus constant, constant plus reciprocal power, constant minus power, and derivative-to-antiderivative blank; q-113781 is explicitly hard. Unlabelled q-2159 and q-29828 are source families but not independently labelled moderate.

invariants: Two summands, power-rule exponents other than -1; no logarithms, substitution, products, definite bounds or integration conditions.
Keep per-item workload near two elementary power integrals.
Retain source answer contract per reproduced source; justify any correction from source evidence.
Power terms have unit magnitude coefficients in target KP examples; arbitrary nonunit coefficients on nonconstant powers belong to the subsequent KP.
permitted_variations: Integration variable, small exponents within supported radical/reciprocal/polynomial classes, constant magnitude, signs and summand order can vary while preserving the method.
The nonconstant term need not remain first or have a fixed sign; the constant and both transformed coefficients are answer-bearing assignments.
Radio answer position and distractor order must not provide an incidental answer cue.
Equivalent radical and rational-power answer forms are defensible; do not use text form alone as a universal correct-choice signal.
